newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia lists U.S. firms for radar planes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia lists U.S. firms for radar planes.

text.p: The Australian government said on Monday it had shortlisted the Boeing Company, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman and Raytheon E-Systems to supply airborne early warning and control aircraft for the Royal Australian Air Force.
"The four shortlisted companies will be invited later this year to respond to a request for proposals," Defence Minister Ian MacLachlan said in a statement.

Lockkheed Martin and Northrop Grumman intended to make a joint proposal for the requirement but requested that they be considered separately until their teaming arrangements were finalised, the minister said.
"Involvement by Australian industry in the project (will) be a key factor in further development of an AEW&C (airborne early warning and control) capability," he said.
"The number of aircraft eventually acquired will be determined once the performance and cost of potential competing systems are known."
Airborne early warning aircraft mount large radars and the necessary computers and communications equipment to process their data.
A Defence Department spokesman said Australia would buy at least four aircraft initially and perhaps more later.
